title: Sancristóbal 2022 · Looming-sound tactile detection
citation: Sancristóbal et al. (2022). Slow Resting State Fluctuations Enhance Neuronal and Behavioral Responses to Looming Sounds. Brain Topography, 35(1), 121–141.
notes: Published study settings are available for inspection. See the source-backed method and remaining execution requirements.

published_method.audio: A 44.1 kHz pink noise sample lasts 3100 ms. The approach variant increases exponentially from 55 to 70 dB SPL. The flat variant is 62.5 dB SPL.
published_method.touch: Single 100 µs rectangular monophasic DS7A pulse on the dorsal right index finger, with individually validated suprathreshold settings.
published_method.response: Speeded left-index Cedrus RB-834 response for touch, withhold on auditory-only. Compare RT for looming and flat sound.
published_method.other_acquisition: An eyes-closed and unstimulated resting EEG assessment preceded the passive auditory task on day 2.

stimulus_type.value: Pink noise with a constant or increasing SPL envelope

catch_count.source: Sancristóbal et al., author-shared journal PDF, PDF p. 5, Behavioral Audio-Tactile Task
catch_count.gap: Five delays × two sound conditions × 18 trials = 180 targets. 180 / 0.60 = 300 trials. The 40% complement is 120 catch trials. Three equally sized blocks give 100 trials per block. The split by sound and target allocation per block are unspecified.

implementation_gaps: Requires the matched dry noise and exact intensity envelopes with physical audio calibration, right-index electrical stimulation and synchronized Cedrus responses.
Audit identifies inconsistent current/voltage terminology. Delivered waveform and per-block allocation by sound are unresolved.
reference_parameters.planner_scope: The study settings describe the source procedure. The Planner contains no executable trial schedule for this profile.
